skill.name: vaex
skill.description: Use Vaex to analyze tabular datasets that exceed memory. The skill covers lazy DataFrames, file conversion, visualization, and machine learning workflows.
skill.summary: Analyze massive tabular datasets with Vaex lazy DataFrames.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples and Vaex performance terminology. Real concerns are unsafe documentation patterns for network binding and cloud credential handling.

remediation.issue: Vaex server example binds to all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Use localhost by default and add access-control guidance before showing public network binding.

remediation.issue: S3 example shows credentials passed directly in code.
remediation.suggestion: Replace hardcoded key examples with environment variables, IAM roles, or provider credential chains.

remediation.issue: GCS example references a local credentials JSON file without safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to commit credential files and prefer managed identity or default credentials.

content.value_statement: Large tabular datasets often exceed memory and slow normal DataFrame tools. This skill gives Vaex patterns for lazy analysis, conversion, visualization, and ML workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading large CSV, HDF5, Arrow, Parquet, and FITS files with Vaex.
Explains lazy expressions, virtual columns, filters, and groupby aggregations.
Recommends conversion, chunking, caching, and delayed execution for performance.
Covers heatmaps, histograms, scatter plots, selections, and subplot workflows.
Outlines Vaex ML preprocessing, encoding, clustering, and model integration.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run Vaex by itself.
It assumes Python and Vaex, so it is not suited for non-tabular data.
Cloud access still depends on local permissions, storage, and credentials.
Some APIs may differ across Vaex versions, so verify installed package behavior.

use_cases.title: Convert Large Data Exports
use_cases.description: Plan a repeatable workflow that converts large CSV exports into faster HDF5 or Arrow datasets.

use_cases.title: Build Memory-Safe Analysis
use_cases.description: Create lazy feature engineering, filtering, and aggregation steps that avoid pandas memory limits.

use_cases.title: Explore Scientific Data
use_cases.description: Generate density plots, summaries, and selections for large astronomical, financial, or research tables.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vaex Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a Vaex workflow to open my large CSV, inspect columns, convert it to HDF5, and compute basic summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Aggregations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Vaex aggregation plan and suggest lazy expressions, virtual columns, and delayed execution steps for better performance.

prompt_templates.title: Design Big Data Visuals
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create Vaex heatmaps and selection-based plots for a large table with x, y, category, and value columns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an ML Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an out-of-core Vaex ML pipeline with encoding, scaling, train-test splitting, model integration, and safe export steps.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to reduce memory use when analyzing a 200 GB CSV.
output: A recommendation to convert the CSV to HDF5 or Arrow once.
A lazy analysis plan using virtual columns and delayed aggregations.
Warnings to avoid full pandas conversion for repeated work.

output_examples.input: A user wants visual summaries for billions of rows.
output: A plot plan using Vaex aggregation grids and density views.
Guidance on limits, shapes, color maps, and selections.
Export suggestions for presentation or further analysis.

output_examples.input: A user needs features for a large machine learning dataset.
output: A preprocessing sequence using virtual columns and Vaex ML transformers.
Advice on categorical encoders, scaling, and compatible model libraries.
Notes on version checks and reproducible pipeline state.

best_practices: Convert repeated large CSV workflows to HDF5 or Arrow before iterative analysis.
Keep derived values as virtual columns until materialization is necessary.
Batch expensive statistics with delayed execution and check memory before export.
anti_patterns: Loading huge datasets into pandas before converting to Vaex.
Hardcoding cloud credentials in scripts or notebook examples.
Binding data servers to all network interfaces without access controls.

faq.question: What is Vaex best for?
faq.answer: Vaex is best for large tabular datasets that exceed memory and need fast lazy analysis.

faq.question: Can this skill process my data directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Which formats should I use with Vaex?
faq.answer: HDF5 and Arrow are usually preferred because Vaex can load them quickly with memory mapping.

faq.question: Does the skill cover visualization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers heatmaps, histograms, scatter plots, selections, and plot layout guidance.

faq.question: Does the skill cover machine learning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Vaex ML transformers, encoders, clustering, and integration with common model libraries.

faq.question: How should I handle cloud credentials?
faq.answer: Use managed credentials, environment variables, or provider credential chains instead of hardcoded secrets.
